done_when: When a review loop stops again after an earlier recorded choice, forge close --resolve narrow, split or accept records the new choice and the board and forge next show the item waiting on that choice until it is made

findings.body: Raise: Functional. An existing client can upgrade after recording its first choice. Earlier same-file stops have no `round` field, so line 194 treats that choice as round zero. The prior three blocked reviews still satisfy `_three_blocked_reviews`, and the first `forge close` after the upgrade stops before reviewing the owner's new work. Earlier any-file stops instead store the attempted fourth round, delaying the next stop by a round. The new test upgrades clients before their first choice, so it misses both persisted-state cases.
findings.title: Earlier-release choices can trigger another stop before three new rounds

why: After the owner records a choice on a stopped review loop, the next stop three rounds later refuses a new choice, so the owner's decision can't be recorded
